question.prompt: The symbol \(|a|\) means \(+a\) if \(a\) is greater than or equal to zero, and \(-a\) if \(a\) is less than or equal to zero; the symbol \(\lt\) means “less than”; the symbol \(\gt\) means “greater than.” The set of values \(x\) satisfying the inequality \(|3-x|\lt4\) consists of all \(x\) such that:

solutions.explanation:
Absolute value measures distance, so \(|3-x|=|x-3|\) is the distance between \(x\) and \(3\) on the number line. A distance less than \(4\) places \(x\) strictly between the points \(4\) units to either side of \(3\):
\[
3-4<x<3+4.
\]
Thus \(-1<x<7\). Both endpoints are excluded because each gives \(|3-x|=4\), while every point between them has distance less than \(4\). The answer is choice D.
solutions.title: Distance from 3
